blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo usar o Future Perfect Continuous (will have been -ing) para falar da duração de uma ação até um ponto futuro e contrastá-lo com o Future Perfect e o Future Continuous, e usar constrain.

body: Esta aula treina **ler textos curtos e achar informação (IELTS Reading, TOEFL Reading)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Negotiation Skills Intensive: Seats Still Open
lines: By the time the course ends in June, you **will have been practising** real bargaining scenarios for twelve weeks. By then our facilitators **will have been coaching** executives for two decades, and they **will have run** over four hundred simulations.
Time pressure and budget cuts often **constrain** what a team can offer, so you will learn to expand the pie. Next month at this time, you **will be sitting** in your first mock mediation.
Register before the 30th: sessions fill quickly.

items.q: Facilitators have only just begun coaching.
Participants will attend a real mediation next month.

frames.title: Future Perfect Continuous: duração até um ponto futuro

head: Estrutura
Exemplo
Ideia
rows: By June, we **will have been negotiating** for a year.
By June, we **will have signed** the deal.
blocks.cap: Future Perfect Continuous: duração até um ponto futuro

blocks.body: Use o **Future Perfect Continuous** quando importa **por quanto tempo** algo vai estar acontecendo (**for / since / by the time**). Verbos de estado não aceitam -ing: use o Future Perfect.
Não use com verbos de estado: *will have been knowing* ✗ → **will have known** ✓.

items.s: By June they ___ for a year. (negotiate)
Budget cuts often ___ what a team can offer. (constrain)
By then she ___ the firm for ten years. (lead, FPC)
By Friday we ___ the contract. (sign, Future Perfect)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Expand the pie.** — Ampliar o ganho comum.
**Hold all the cards.** — Ter a vantagem total.
**Play your cards close to the chest.** — Jogar de forma reservada.
**Come to the table.** — Sentar-se para negociar.
**Meet halfway.** — Chegar a um meio-termo.
**Put cards on the table.** — Abrir o jogo.
**Bargain from strength.** — Barganhar de posição de força.
**Cut one’s losses.** — Reduzir as perdas.
**Time is of the essence.** — O tempo é essencial.
**Twelve weeks, mostly in simulations.** — Doze semanas, principalmente em simulações.
**How long will you have been practising by June?** — Há quanto tempo você estará praticando em junho?
**Will the facilitators have finished their own training by then?** — Os facilitadores terão terminado o próprio treinamento até lá?

items.label: Ênfase intencional
items.note: Ênfase intencional: você escolhe qual palavra recebe o acento principal para marcar contraste ou informação nova (nuclear stress).
words: I said we need a DEAL.
We need a DEAL, not a delay.
It’s not the PRICE, it’s the TERMS.

prompts.q: Say how long you will have been studying English by next year.
prompts.model: By next year, I will have been studying English for ten years.
I will have been writing for hours; I will have finished the draft.
Time constrains what I can promise.

blocks.task: Write 5 sentences about what you will have been doing by the end of this year.
blocks.model: By December, I will have been working in this team for five years. I will have been negotiating supplier contracts since March. By then, my colleagues will have been using the new system for months. Budgets will still constrain what we can offer. I hope we will have signed the deal.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
